target_customer: Corporate teams, people teams, executive assistants and event marketers who plan offsites, kickoffs and meetings, from startups to large enterprises
problem: Planning corporate events means weeks of emailing venues, comparing long hotel proposals and managing vendors. Nowadays uses AI to source venues, contact them, compare proposals and track budgets.
business_model: Event planning platform and service, commercial terms not stated in sources opened
product_category: AI corporate meetings and events planning

founders.name: Anna Sun
founders.background_notes: YC page lists PM and software engineer roles at those employers.

founders.name: Amy Yan
founders.background_notes: Older sister of Anna Sun per TechCrunch; strategy and operations roles per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Calling and emailing venues with LLMs and parsing long proposals was feasible with 2023 language models, but multilingual voice calling and reliable negotiation take real engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Venue data and vendor relationships can build up, but the workflow could be copied by event incumbents and other startups using the same models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch in December 2024 says Cvent and Eventbrite were adding AI tools; no acquisition of Nowadays found.

market_need_then: Corporate event planning was manual and slow. The company cites 20 to 30 percent savings versus booking direct, from its own site, and early use by startups; demand evidence at founding is mostly founder experience planning large events.

identity.mascot_or_character: A dog in a party hat appears on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: casual and friendly with emojis and short direct headlines

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly playful identity on the site and some trade press coverage, but no evidence of community, merch or brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Nowadays started with small startups and moved toward enterprise customers, with its site listing large logos. It raised a $2M seed in December 2024 after saying fundraising was hard. AI language models made automated venue outreach newly feasible, which helped timing, while incumbents and other AI event startups are a continuing threat.
notes: A web interview snippet says the company began with a $500k YC check; not recorded as a round since YC standard deal. An aggregator snippet listing a $7M seed in 2022 predates founding and is rejected. No dated 2023 competitor source was opened, so the competitor list is empty; Cvent, Eventbrite and Partiful are named only in a December 2024 article. Company site says 'Built by MIT engineers'.
